title: Website Redesign
body:
Overview

I have redesigned my personal website to improve its overall appearance and presentation of my projects. As a recent software engineering graduate, I wanted my portfolio to reflect my skills while providing visitors with a clean, intuitive, and responsive browsing experience.

In this post, I’ll walk through my goals behind the redesign, the changes I made to the layout and visual styling, and how I approached responsive design to create a consistent experience across different screen sizes.


The Original Design

The original version of my personal website serves as a place to showcase my software development projects and share my thoughts, experiences, moments from my life, and more. Currently, the portfolio contains two projects, while the blog contains only one post.

As I reviewed the existing frontend, I wanted to consider how the website presents this content and how its layout, navigation, and visual styling could be improved. Rather than focusing solely on the amount of content available, I wanted the redesign to establish a clearer visual hierarchy and make existing blog posts and projects easier to discover.

This provided an opportunity for me to rethink how I want the website’s layout and presentation to look while maintaining its purpose as my personal portfolio.

Areas of Focus:

  • Content presentation: Improve how the two portfolio projects and published blog post are displayed.
  • Layout and Spacing: Establish a clear visual hierarchy and make better use of available screen space.
  • Visual Consistency: Create a cohesive style across the homepage, portfolio, and blog.
  • Navigation and responsiveness: Make the website easier to navigate and more comfortable to use across different screen sizes.

The New Design

The redesigned version of my personal website focuses on improving the overall visual presentation, layout, and user experience. I wanted to create a more cohesive design that makes my portfolio and blog easier to navigate while maintaining a consistent appearance throughout the website.

Overall:

I have added the background image for my current desktop setup, which in my case is my graduation picture. I have also added a sitemap with recent blog posts and projects at the bottom of each page, replacing the social media placeholder.

Homepage:

The homepage serves as the main introduction to my personal website. The redesign focuses on presenting information clearly, establishing a consistent visual identity, and helping visitors navigate to the portfolio and blog. I have added the recent posts and projects and moved the feedback form to a different page.

Blog:

The blog serves as a place to share my thoughts, experiences, and updates from my journey as a developer. This redesign focuses on better placement of posts. I have added the recent posts to this page as well. For each post, the background image is replaced with the post’s image. The post detail section appears on the left and recent posts on the right.

Portfolio:

The portfolio serves as a place to share my projects that I have built as a developer. This redesign focuses on better placement of projects. I have added the recent projects to this page as well. I have also redesigned the detail section for each project. For each project, such as Bit Shifter Test, the background image is replaced with the project’s image. The detail section of the project appears on the left with a button linking to the source code right below the description. The recent projects appear on the right.

About:

The About page serves as a place for more information about me, my background, and my interest in software development, along with information about the website and a way to contact me for issues, bugs, security concerns, and more. I have moved the feedback page from the home page to the About page and added a contact section with my email.

What’s next?

I plan to build a learning path to keep learning and improving as a software developer.


Conclusion

The redesign primarily focused on improving the layout and visual styling while introducing additional functionality like recent posts and projects. I’ve updated the CSS to support the new design and improve usability.

Alongside the visual changes, I added the recent blog posts and projects to the home page, footer, projects page, and blog page.
